state: A company-internal application language, Can, has editable design drafts rather than a compatibility-constraining implementation. AI authors its programs. Success is judged by adoption, minimal redundant source, clear desired JavaScript and a single consistent expression of an operation. Its structure separates declarations and constraints in Given, guarded business behavior in When, and screens in Then. Today an imported typed service capability specifies inputs and eventual outputs. send commits a durable request and yields a delivery association, with later completion processing. Incremental content, ongoing job status and cancel requests do not yet have agreed typed semantics. The runtime substrate already includes fetch, encoding, streams and crypto through workerd, and hosted Cloudflare offers separate bound database/object storage, model inference and workflow services. Existing JavaScript packages can supply reusable implementation. Intended new examples cover standard LLM chat, Ollama conversations connected to ComfyUI generation via one binding of prompt/negative prompt/width/height to concrete node inputs, JEV SystemONE's NOUL/choice/score classifications including uncertainty, departmental email sorting, and finite recurring searches whose cited opportunities are reviewed before CRM acceptance. Output-shape support, tools, partial output, stopping and replay vary across providers. Shared code can handle protocols and bytes; business authors still decide routing, research sources, decision criteria, which actions require approval and allowed spending. No benchmark or complete implementation establishes the relative merits. Advice is sought about which boundary to investigate first, leaving syntax provisional and not assuming support for all vendor options.

boundary.instructions: Recommend the first design hypothesis to evaluate for the described workloads, balancing source economy, meaning preservation, provider variability, adapter upkeep and compiler versus library obligations. Treat all candidates as unverified and do not preserve current restrictions solely because they already appear in drafts.

criteria.generic: Retain one general external-operation contract with shared incremental-status and cancel semantics added as examples require. Model each vendor through its own typed request and response declarations, without standard schemas for the AI and media families. This keeps distinct provider features explicit and allows common execution plumbing, while leaving more provider-shaped data and repeated domain configuration in consuming apps.
criteria.shared: Use ordinary imports to access standard typed interfaces for text generation, decision classification, searching/retrieval and image work. Investigate language-wide stream/resumption behavior as demonstrated by examples, with explicit adapter support differences. This centralizes reusable semantics without vendor-specific syntax, while creating real work to define abstractions, lifecycle guarantees and unsupported-capability behavior.
criteria.dedicated: Give generative models, classification models and media workflows their own core declarations and execution rules, incorporating endpoint options and node mappings into those forms. Direct notation can be short and offer domain-specific checks; the tradeoff is more grammar and continuing semantic maintenance, plus ensuring these forms do not create competing ways to invoke ordinary services.
